paper_title: Diketopyrrolopyrrole-Coumarin Conjugates for Efficient Binary Organic Solar Cells

knowledge_points.content: Two coumarin-functionalized diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP) derivatives, asymmetric DPP-Cou and symmetric Cou-DPP-Cou, were synthesized using Suzuki-type cross-coupling reactions between brominated DPP and coumarin boronic esters.
knowledge_points.evidence: The synthesized compound 3 was reacted with bromo-derivatives 5 and 6 under Suzuki-type cross-coupling reaction conditions to give the final compounds DPP-Cou and Cou-DPP-Cou in 45-50% yield.

knowledge_points.content: Symmetric Cou-DPP-Cou exhibits a lower optical bandgap (1.67 eV) and red-shifted absorption (up to ~750 nm) compared to asymmetric DPP-Cou (1.78 eV, ~700 nm) due to extended pi-conjugation from the additional coumarin unit.
knowledge_points.evidence: The extension of the molecular backbone by an additional coumarin derivative in symmetrical Cou-DPP-Cou extends the absorption to ~750 nm (Eg opt = 1.67 eV) compared to ~700 nm (Eg opt = 1.78 eV) for asymmetric DPP-Cou.

knowledge_points.content: Symmetric Cou-DPP-Cou demonstrates higher thermal stability than asymmetric DPP-Cou, with a 5% weight loss temperature of 340 °C compared to 230 °C for the latter, attributed to higher crystallinity and better molecular packing.
knowledge_points.evidence: Cou-DPP-Cou shows high thermal stability with 5% weight loss at around 340 °C, while DPP-Cou starts to decompose with 5% weight loss at 230 °C... related to the higher crystallinity and better molecular packing of the former.

knowledge_points.content: Binary organic solar cells based on the Cou-DPP-Cou:Y7 blend achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 13.48%, with a short-circuit current (JSC) of 22.86 mA/cm², an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 0.88 V, and a fill factor (FF) of 0.67.
knowledge_points.evidence: Cou-DPP-Cou:Y7 and DPP-Cou:Y7 attained overall power conversion efficiencies (PCE) of 13.48 and 9.63% respectively. (Table 3: Jsc 22.86, Voc 0.88, FF 0.67 for Cou-DPP-Cou:Y7).

knowledge_points.content: Solvent vapor annealing (SVA) treatment using tetrahydrofuran (THF) for 40 seconds was employed to optimize the active layer morphology and improve the efficiency of the Cou-DPP-Cou:Y7 and DPP-Cou:Y7 devices.
knowledge_points.evidence: After optimization using solvent vapor annealing treatment... we have adopted the SVA treatment by exposing the optimized active layer to the vapors of THF solvents for 40 s.

knowledge_points.content: The HOMO and LUMO energy levels for Cou-DPP-Cou are -5.48 eV and -3.75 eV, respectively, while for DPP-Cou they are -5.49 eV and -3.68 eV, providing sufficient driving force for exciton dissociation when paired with the Y7 acceptor.
knowledge_points.evidence: The HOMO/LUMO energy levels of Cou-DPP-Cou and DPP-Cou are estimated from the onset oxidation/reduction potentials are -5.48/-3.75 eV and -5.49/-3.68 eV, respectively... provide a sufficient driving force for exciton dissociation.

knowledge_points.content: Cou-DPP-Cou:Y7 devices exhibit more balanced charge transport than DPP-Cou:Y7, with hole and electron mobilities of 2.04 x 10^-4 cm²/V·s and 2.67 x 10^-4 cm²/V·s, respectively (ratio of 1.31).
knowledge_points.evidence: The μh (2.04 x 10^-4 cm2/V-1 s) and μe (2.67 x 10^-4 cm2/V-1 s) with μe/μh = 1.31 for Cou-DPP-Cou:Y7 blends are higher than that for DPP-Cou:Y7... signifying that the charge transport is more balanced.

knowledge_points.content: Bimolecular recombination is more effectively suppressed in Cou-DPP-Cou:Y7 devices, as indicated by a light-intensity exponent (alpha) of 0.964, which is closer to unity than the 0.929 observed for DPP-Cou:Y7.
knowledge_points.evidence: The estimated alpha values are 0.964 and 0.929 for the device based on Cou-DPP-Cou and DPP-Cou, respectively. The higher alpha value for Cou-DPP-Cou, closer to unity, indicating that bimolecular recombination is suppressed.

knowledge_points.content: X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis shows that the Cou-DPP-Cou:Y7 blend has a more compact pi-pi stacking distance of 0.366 nm and a larger crystal coherence length (CCL) of 2.24 nm compared to the DPP-Cou:Y7 blend.
knowledge_points.evidence: The pi-pi stacking distances for the DPP-Cu:Y7 and Cou-DPP-Cou:Y7 are about 0.372 and 0.366 nm, respectively. The sharper pi-pi stacking peak with larger CCL (2.24 nm) and compact pi-pi distance for Cou-DPP-Cou:Y7 suggests higher crystallinity.

knowledge_points.content: Transient photocurrent (TPC) measurements reveal a faster charge extraction time for Cou-DPP-Cou:Y7 (0.94 microseconds) compared to DPP-Cou:Y7 (1.05 microseconds), facilitating higher short-circuit current.
knowledge_points.evidence: The charge extraction time estimated from the exponential decay of photocurrent are about 0.94 μs for Cou-DPP-Cou and 1.05 μs for DPP-Cou-based devices, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: Density functional theory (DFT) calculations indicate that asymmetric DPP-Cou has a much larger ground-state dipole moment (4.558 Debye) compared to the symmetric Cou-DPP-Cou (0.002 Debye).
knowledge_points.evidence: The ground-state dipole moments (μg) for Cou-DPP-Cou and DPP-Cou are calculated to be 0.002 and 4.558 Debye, respectively... asymmetric DPP-Cou shows the higher dipole moment.

knowledge_points.content: The higher fill factor (FF) in Cou-DPP-Cou-based devices is attributed to reduced energy loss (0.46 eV vs 0.50 eV for DPP-Cou) and higher charge collection probability (0.76 vs 0.712).
knowledge_points.evidence: The Eloss calculated for Cou-DPP-Cou and DPP-Cou are 0.46 and 0.50 eV... The Pcoll values are 0.76 for Cou-DPP-Cou-based OSCs and 0.712 for DPP-Cou-based OSCs.
